panels.figure_caption: Pathologic presentation of a biting fibroma on the lower mucosal lip of an 80-year-old woman Distant (A) and closer (B, C, and D) views of the microscopic features of the biting fibroma from the patient’s lower lip are shown. There is slight thickening (acanthosis) of stratified squamous epithelium (black brackets). The underlying lamina propria contains collagen that is arranged in a radiating pattern (black asterixis). Numerous vessels (black arrows), some containing red blood cells, are also present in the lamina propria (hematoxylin and eosin stain: A, ×4; B, ×10; C, ×20; and D, ×40)
in_text_mentions: The microscopic evaluation of the tissue specimen showed collagenous fibrous tissue with vessels in the lamina propria. The arrangement of the collagen fibers had a radiating pattern, and some of the vessels contained erythrocytes. The overlying stratified squamous epithelium was slightly acanthotic (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Frontal view of a lower lip mucosal papule in an 80-year-old woman; caption and article title explicitly attribute the lesion to an irritation (biting) fibroma arising at the traumatic bite site, with mucosa-colored, smooth, firm surface. B: Left-side view of the same lower lip mucosal papule; caption identifies it as an irritation fibroma at the tooth-bite traumatic site, mucosa-colored and smooth.
panels.attribution_text: Cohen. Biting Fibroma of the Lower Lip: A Case Report and Literature Review on an Irritation Fibroma Occurring at the Traumatic Site of a Tooth Bite.. Cureus 2022. doi:10.7759/cureus.32237. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Biting fibroma presenting as a mucosa-colored papule on the mucosa of the lower lip The frontal view (A) and left-side view (B) of the lower lip mucosa of an 80-year-old woman show an acquired lesion of two years duration. The nontender, firm, flesh-colored, 3 × 3 millimeter smooth papule (black arrow) appeared after she bit her lip at the site
in_text_mentions: The patient assisted in the cutaneous examination of her lower lip. She gently everted the lip with the index and middle fingers from both of her hands. There was a painless, smooth, firm, flesh-colored, 3 × 3 millimeter papule on the mucosal portion of the lower lip, just left of the midline (Figure 1). An excisional biopsy was performed.

plate_findings.evidence: Cytokeratin wide (CK-wide) immunostaining highlights the surface epithelium (internal positive control), while the lesional stroma is negative

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Ki-67 immunohistochemistry of the lesional tissue from a case report titled and diagnosed as denture-related irritation fibroma; the panel shows the lesion's low proliferative activity, an ancillary diagnostic feature supporting the diagnosis, but no morphological feature listed in the vocabulary (the Ki-67 index is a negative/ancillary finding and is therefore proposed rather than mapped). Panel label and 200 µm scale bar are annotated. B: CK-wide immunohistochemistry of the irritation fibroma shows the intact stratified squamous epithelial lining over the lesion (internal positive control) with negative lesional stroma; caption and article title attribute the tissue to denture-related irritation fibroma, supporting the mapped epithelial finding. Panel label and 200 µm scale bar are annotated.
panels.attribution_text: Sato et al. Denture-Related Irritation Fibroma With Myxoid Change of the Anterior Hard Palate: A Clinicopathologic Case Report.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.105604. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: Immunohistochemical findings A) Ki-67 immunostaining shows a very low nuclear labeling index, indicating no increased proliferative activity. B) Cytokeratin wide (CK-wide) immunostaining highlights the surface epithelium (internal positive control), while the lesional stroma is negative. Scale bar: 200 μm
in_text_mentions: Immunohistochemical staining showed a very low Ki-67 labeling index (Figure 5A). The lesional stromal cells were negative for broad-spectrum cytokeratin (CK-wide), whereas the surface epithelium showed diffuse positivity as an internal positive control (Figure 5B). Taken together, these findings, in the clinical setting of chronic denture-related trauma, led to a final diagnosis of denture-related irritation fibroma with myxoid stromal change.

panels.rationale: Single H&E histology panel from an article specifically about a large irritation fibroma of the hard palate. The caption and in-text histopathology description support irritation fibroma with dense fibrous/collagenous connective tissue, stratified squamous epithelium, fibroblasts, and chronic lymphocytic inflammation. Real patient histology image; no third-party copyright indicated.
panels.attribution_text: Srivastava et al. A Large Irritation Fibroma of the Hard Palate: A Rare Clinical Entity.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.62244. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: Histological section slide (10x magnification) Staining used: hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The section shows a surface lined by stratified squamous epithelium, with the bulk of the lesion composed of dense, fibrous connective tissue, with varying degrees of collagen. There is a presence of chronic inflammatory cells, predominantly lymphocytes.
in_text_mentions: The final histopathological examination revealed fibro-collagenous connective tissue with collagen bundles containing fibroblasts. There was a presence of overlying squamous epithelium showing keratin collection. There was no definite evidence of dysplasia/malignancy (Figure 5).

panels.rationale: Single histology panel (H&E, 10x) from a case of large irritation fibroma of the hard palate. Caption and in-text describe stratified squamous epithelium with hyperplasia/hyperkeratosis and a nodular mass of fibrous connective tissue, supporting irritation fibroma. No skin tone assessable; no patient age or ethnicity provided.
panels.attribution_text: Tsikopoulos et al. Large irritation fibroma of hard palate: a case report of a rare clinical entity.. The Pan African medical journal 2021. doi:10.11604/pamj.2021.38.61.27662. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: histopathological feature of the specimen (Zoom 10x), epithelium with hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis
in_text_mentions: The histopathological examination revealed a nodular mass of fibrous connective tissue, covered by stratified squamous epithelium with focal low-medium grade hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis. Beneath the epithelium were spotted many small blood capillaries scattered all over the lesion and mild inflammation. These features were consistent with irritation fibroma (Figure 4, Figure 5). On the follow-up appointments, no signs of recurrence of the tumor were observed and the patient did not mention any further complaint.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Coronal CT of a real patient showing a soft-tissue mass on the right anterior hard palate without cortical erosion, in a case report whose title and diagnosis is denture-related irritation fibroma; the mass is the radiologic manifestation of the lesion, though the finding vocabulary (mucosal/histologic descriptors) does not cover CT appearances. B: Sagittal CT of the same patient confirming the palatal soft-tissue mass with intact palatal bone surface (arrow), consistent with the case report's diagnosis of irritation fibroma of the anterior hard palate.

panels.figure_caption: Computed tomography (CT) findings of the palatal lesion A) Coronal CT image showing a soft-tissue mass on the right anterior hard palate without cortical erosion of the palatal bone. B) Sagittal CT image confirming the absence of underlying bony resorption beneath the lesion; the arrow indicates the intact palatal bone surface.
in_text_mentions: dysphagia or speech difficulty, aside from awareness of the mass. The lesion was freely movable on palpation, with an elastic to slightly firm consistency, and no induration was detected. The maxillary complete denture had been fabricated with relief of the palatal base to accommodate the external contour of the lesion (Figure 1B). Helical computed tomography (CT) of the maxilla demonstrated a soft-tissue mass on the right anterior hard palate, without cortical erosion or resorption of the underlying palatal bone (Figures 2A-2B). There was no involvement of the nasal floor or maxillary sinus.
